title: Start or schedule task run
description: Start a cloud run for an existing task, or set `scheduled_at` for a one-off run within 30 days. Times without an offset use UTC. Confirm the returned time; execution starts at or after that time. Omit model fields to use saved defaults, or the previous run's model on resume. Use `tasks-models-retrieve` before an explicit model choice. Use `pending_user_message` for follow-up work and `resume_from_run_id` to continue a prior run. The created run is the top-level `run`; read `run.id` for run-scoped calls — the top-level `id` is the task's. Poll `tasks-runs-list` or `tasks-runs-retrieve` for progress. Check `run_error` for a start failure. If the response is lost, check the runs before you retry. A repeated call can start another run.

methodDocumentation.text: Create a new task run and kick off the workflow. The response is the refreshed task with the created run under the top-level `run` key: read `run.id` for anything run-scoped, such as the run's stream and command endpoints. The top-level `id` is the task's, and `latest_run` mirrors `run` only as long as nothing newer starts — reading either of those as the created run is deprecated.

typeDocumentation.effectiveDescription:
The task ``run`` action's response: the refreshed task detail plus the run this call made.

``run`` is the run the call created or activated — the payload a caller reads run-scoped ids
from, instead of inferring them from ``latest_run`` (or, worse, the top-level task ``id``).
